name: 200-day MA Timing (Meb Faber tactical rule)
description: Long the main US index when price is above its 200-day moving average, out (to cash) when below. One parameter, ~century of history. Pitched as 'dilution of signal, cutting variance' — the classic risk-reduction overlay.
instrument: S&P 500 (^GSPC for history, SPY to trade)

setup.description: signal = close > SMA(200). Long when true, hold cash (earning risk-free) when false.

exit.cash: price closes below the 200-day MA -> to T-bills

verdict.claim: beats the market with lower volatility over a 92-year test; not overfit
verdict.result_long_history_1960_2026: MA200 +15,573% vs buy-and-hold +12,390%, max drawdown -22% vs ~-55% (2008). Claim HOLDS — higher return AND half the drawdown.
verdict.result_recent_bull_2020: MA200 +114% vs buy-and-hold +152%. LAGS in bull markets (sits out dips, misses V-recoveries) — the caveat he omits.
verdict.honest_take: Legitimately good risk-reduction overlay with real academic support; the low-overfitting claim is FAIR (one parameter, long history). Its edge is drawdown control + long-run compounding of cash yield when out — NOT beating bull markets. Depends on idle cash earning the risk-free rate.
verdict.engine_note: This strategy exposed a real flaw: the engine earned 0% when out of market, badly under-crediting sit-in-cash strategies. Fixed — idle capital now accrues RISK_FREE_RATE, and Sharpe is now excess-of-risk-free. MA200's measured return jumped from +6,892% to +15,573% after the fix.
